\[
\boxed{(\ell-1)^r\ell^{2qr}\,
\frac{(2q)!}{\left(\frac{2q-1}{\ell^r}+1\right)!\left(\left(\frac{2q-1}{\ell^r}\right)!\right)^{\ell^r-1}}}
\]

Let \(V=\mathbb F_\ell^r\), \(N=2q\), and \(L=|V|=\ell^r\). Since \(2q\equiv1\pmod{\ell^r}\), write
\[
t=\frac{2q-1}{\ell^r},
\qquad N=tL+1.
\]

For a lift \(\sigma\) of the fixed permutation \(\pi\), write
\[
\sigma(\rho_j)=\zeta^{c_j}\rho_j,\qquad
\sigma(\alpha_i^{(j)})=\zeta^{b_i^{(j)}}\alpha_{\pi(i)}^{(j)}.
\]
The condition \(\sigma(\rho_j)\ne\rho_j\) is exactly \(c_j\ne0\), giving \((\ell-1)^r\) choices for \(c=(c_1,\dots,c_r)\).

The product relation \(\prod_i\alpha_i^{(j)}\in M\) imposes one affine linear condition on the \(b_i^{(j)}\) for each \(j\). Thus for each \(j\), after grouping the \(n=4q\) indices into the \(N=2q\) transposition-pairs of \(\pi\), define
\[
B_A^{(j)}=b_x^{(j)}+b_{\pi(x)}^{(j)}
\]
for the pair \(A=\{x,\pi(x)\}\). The total \(\sum_A B_A^{(j)}\) is fixed. Once the \(B_A^{(j)}\) are chosen, each transposition-pair has \(\ell\) choices for splitting \(B_A^{(j)}\) into the two \(b\)-values. Across all \(j\), this contributes \(\ell^{Nr}=\ell^{2qr}\).

Now consider an element of \(\Omega_k\) indexed by \((i,h,u)\), where \(h\notin\{i,\pi(i)\}\). Under \(\sigma\),
\[
u_j\mapsto u_j+k_jc_j+b_i^{(j)}-2b_h^{(j)}.
\]
The base map \((i,h)\mapsto(\pi(i),\pi(h))\) has order \(2\). After applying it twice, the translation in the \(j\)-th coordinate is
\[
2k_jc_j+\bigl(b_i^{(j)}+b_{\pi(i)}^{(j)}\bigr)
-2\bigl(b_h^{(j)}+b_{\pi(h)}^{(j)}\bigr).
\]
So for ordered transposition-pairs \(A\ne B\), the relevant vector is
\[
2kc+B_A-2B_B\in V.
\]
A two-step translation by \(0\) gives cycles of length \(2\); a nonzero translation gives cycles of length \(2\ell\). Therefore the cycle type depends only on the number of ordered pair-orbits for which
\[
B_A-2B_B=-2kc.
\]
Because every \(c_j\ne0\), the map \(k\mapsto 2kc\) is a bijection of \(V\). Hence the cycle types are the same for all \(k\) iff the values
\[
B_A-2B_B,\qquad A\ne B,
\]
are uniformly distributed over \(V\).

Let \(m_x\) be the number of transposition-pairs \(A\) with \(B_A=x\). Uniformity says
\[
\sum_y m_{v+2y}m_y-m_{-v}
\]
is independent of \(v\). Taking Fourier transforms on \(V\), for every nontrivial character \(\chi\),
\[
M(\chi)M(\chi^{-2})=M(\chi^{-1}),
\qquad
M(\chi)=\sum_x m_x\chi(x).
\]
Since \(N=tL+1\equiv1\pmod \ell\), each \(M(\chi)\equiv1\) modulo \(1-\zeta\), so \(M(\chi)\ne0\). Thus \(|M(\chi)|=1\) for every nontrivial \(\chi\).

Now set \(m_x=t+\varepsilon_x\). Then \(\sum_x\varepsilon_x=1\), and the nontrivial Fourier coefficients of \(\varepsilon\) all have absolute value \(1\), while the trivial one is \(1\). Parseval gives
\[
\sum_x \varepsilon_x^2=\frac1L\sum_\chi |\widehat\varepsilon(\chi)|^2=1.
\]
Since the \(\varepsilon_x\) are integers and sum to \(1\), exactly one \(\varepsilon_x\) equals \(1\), and all others are \(0\). Thus the \(B_A\)'s must take every value of \(V\) exactly \(t\) times, with one value occurring \(t+1\) times. The fixed total sum determines which value is the exceptional one.

Therefore the number of valid assignments of the \(N=2q\) labeled transposition-pairs is
\[
\frac{(2q)!}{(t+1)!(t!)^{L-1}}.
\]
Multiplying by the \(\ell^{2qr}\) splitting choices and the \((\ell-1)^r\) choices of \(c\), the required number is
\[
\boxed{(\ell-1)^r\ell^{2qr}\,
\frac{(2q)!}{\left(\frac{2q-1}{\ell^r}+1\right)!\left(\left(\frac{2q-1}{\ell^r}\right)!\right)^{\ell^r-1}}}.
\]
